documentNotes.statement: The separately named participant answer sheet is not present as an independent file. The complete blank examiner report is retained with problem 10; its star list includes Arcturus, Fomalhaut, α Centauri, Sirius, Vega, Deneb, Procyon, Antares, Altair and Spica. No answers or observations are inferred.

Three whole independent tasks8–10 with printed subparts and group-specific targets. Full chart and examiner form retained; participant answer sheet separate file absent; no completed observing key. Both actual final image assets personally inspected: full sky chart and complete original-byte examiner report.

problems.statement: Given in a separate “answer sheet” are 10 of the brighter stars in the night sky.

parts.statement: In the table (see answer sheet), mark by X the squares in the last column for those stars that **are visible to you now**.
Show them to the examiner with the help of a torch beam.
Point out the Vernal Equinox in the sky.

problems.statement:
Please refer to the sky-chart given to you. The chart shows a part of tonight’s sky in the orientation as you can see it now. The positions of planets Uranus and Neptune are marked in the chart.

![](p9-skychart)

parts.statement: Both the planets are not easily visible to the naked eye. Point, in the sky, the stars closest to these planets.
Estimate the angular distance between the Uranus and the Neptune (write value on the answer sheet).

problems.statement:
You have been given a 125-mm Newtonian reflecting telescope, focal length $F=1025$ mm, on an azimuth mount with a set of 3 eye pieces. The focal lengths of the eyepieces are: 12 mm, 25 mm and 38 mm.

The target for you depends on group:

(α): Pleiades – Плеяды

(β): Albireo (binary) – Альбирео (двойная)

Choose suitable eyepiece, bring the target to the centre of the field of view of the telescope and show it to the examiner.
